functions/SpawnDamageNumberEffect.asm.blockNote:
Floating damage-number actor (Bank 00, 56500-56579). One spawn is one 16-frame effect: it draws the damage value as digit sprites above the victim and lets them rise one pixel per frame while following the victim's own movement. The old name (SpawnAttackTrailEffect, 'attack trail') and the old text ('ghost copies interpolated between the previous and current position', '16 frames at position then 16 drifting upward', 'when the player or enemies take damage') do not describe it: there is one 16-iteration loop and no ghost copies.

=== SPAWN ===

Two sites in combat_collision: COP SpawnListAppend ( @SpawnDamageNumberEffect, #00, #00, flags ) in PlayerAttackHitTest with flags $2F00, and in ApplyHitDamageToVictim_DamagePath with flags $2B00 (that path then ORs $1000 into the child's $12). The fourth operand is the flags word stored into the child's $10, not a priority. Both sites run with the victim as the current actor, so CopyActorState gives the child the victim's X and Y and stores the victim's slot in the child's $24. The caller then writes the packed BCD damage from FormatDamageDigits into the child's $28.
No child is spawned when the victim's $12 bit $0020 (boss) is set or when the damage is 1000 or more (FormatDamageDigits returns carry). No other spawn site exists in extracted/.

=== BODY ===

1. $0E := $3200: the attribute word ORed into every digit tile (OAM high byte $32 = priority 3, palette 1).
2. $16 -= $10: start 16 pixels above the victim.
3. Y := $24 (the victim); remember its X and Y in $20 and $22.
4. 16 iterations (LoopStart #10 = 16): add the victim's X movement since last frame to $14, add its Y movement minus 1 to $16 (so the digits rise one pixel per frame), refresh $20/$22, copy $28 to the absolute scratch word $0000 and call ComposeDigitSprites. ComposeDigitSprites puts the first digit at $14 - 12 and appends one 6-byte entry per digit to the compose buffer at $7F3100. LoopEnd yields every iteration, so the digits are re-emitted every frame; then Die.

The scratch word is written with the absolute address $0000 on purpose: it is not the actor's own $00/$01 re-entry address.

=== HAZARD ===

The loop re-reads the victim's position through $24 every frame and never checks that the slot still holds the same actor. If the victim died and its slot were reused within the 16 frames, the number would follow whatever occupies the slot (analysis only, not run; OQ-I041-5).

DamageNumberShort_unused is an unreferenced variant of this routine.

unused/DamageNumberShort_unused.asm.blockNote:
Unreferenced shortened variant of SpawnDamageNumberEffect (formerly AttackTrailShort_unused).

Composes only 4 upward digit-sprite frames plus 32 more (vs 16+16), with a smaller Y offset ($FFF8). Would have rendered a shorter floating damage number. Never called by combat_collision or any actor script.

actors/hit_switch.asm.blockNote:
Hit switch (Bank 00, 51710-51778; formerly named floor_button): a solid, hit-triggered switch that raises one numbered event flag each time it is struck. It is not a pressure plate: the actor is solid (MarkSolidHere), so the player cannot stand on it, and the trigger is the engine's hit callback. The old text ('triggers puzzle state when the player or objects land on the plate', 'used in pyramid puzzle rooms') is wrong.

=== INIT ===

actor-def <#00,#00,#01>. $24 := $0E (spawn type byte >> 1, the flag number), then $0E := $2000 (OAM attribute word, priority 2). statsPtr points at enemy_stats_table + $118 (the assembler's offset is hex), which is entry $46: HP $14, ATK $16, DEF $FF, type 0; the actor's currentHp is overwritten with $FF anyway. Metasprite spriteset_enemies, frame $0F shown with AnimOnce, MarkSolidHere. $12 |= $0031: bit $0001 selects between the two post-hit invulnerability modes ($FFEF recovery vs $0011 invincibility in combat_collision; which one it picks was not traced), bit $0010 makes the victim stagger-immune, bit $0020 marks it as a boss so no damage digits are spawned (combat_collision).
HitSwitchRearm (re-arm): currentHp := $FF, COP SetHitCallback ( &HitSwitchTriggered ), SetEntryHere, RTL. The actor then idles.

=== WHEN HIT ===

combat_collision dispatches onHitCallback ($7F1000) after the hit damage: the callback pointer becomes the victim's entry address and onHitCallback is cleared, so the script below runs on the actor's next turn. HitSwitchTriggered: SetFlagRaw with A = $24 (the event-flag number, no base offset), frame $10 (assumed to be the pressed look; not viewed), AnimOnce, WaitByte #0F, frame $0F, AnimOnce, then BRA HitSwitchRearm which restores HP $FF and registers the callback again. The button can therefore be struck again after about $0F frames plus two animation cycles.

=== PLACEMENT AND FLAG READERS ===

Seven spawns, all in Great Wall scenes (the old docs say pyramid):

| Scene | Area | Position (tile) | Type byte | Flag | Reader of that flag |
|-------|------|-----------------|-----------|------|---------------------|
| 83 | great_wall/wall_dive | 35,1B | 03 | $01 | gw83_switch (WaitOnFlagByte $01, placed on the same tile) |
| 85 | great_wall/wall_rampway | 18,1A | 03 | $01 | gw85_retractable_gate |
| 85 | great_wall/wall_rampway | 3B,29 and 29,2B | 05 | $02 | gw85_short_switch_spear |
| 85 | great_wall/wall_rampway | 37,2C | 07 | $03 | gw85_long_switch_spear |
| 85 | great_wall/wall_rampway | 64,1D | 09 | $04 | gw85_multi_switch_spear |
| 87 | scene 87 (no area folder in extracted/) | 2F,28 | 1F | $0F | none in the scene's spawn list |

The gw85 actors run WaitOnFlagByte ( #n, #01 ) followed by ClearFlagByte ( #n ), so in the rampway the flag is a one-shot trigger consumed by the gate or spear. gw83_switch waits on flag $01 and does not clear it. In scene 87 the flag $0F has no waiter among the scene's actors (the gw82_wall_spear actors it spawns use timers only); $0F is also used as an unrelated flag in Babel Tower and Freejia scripts (OQ-I042-3).

functions/EnemyDropSystem.asm.blockNote:
Enemy drop spawner for gems and heals (Bank 00, 57129-57340). The old names (DarkGemDropSystem, SpawnDarkGemType1 and so on) said 'dark gem', but what drops is a pickup carrying item id $83 to $86 of GiveItemToPlayer: 1, 2 or 5 gems, or a 5 HP heal.

=== CALLER ===

StandardEnemyDefeatHandler reaches EnemyGemDropRouter when the defeated enemy's stat byte +3 (enemy-stats gemDropType) is nonzero and scene flag $0300 is clear. The router spawns one of three entries with SpawnListAppend (flags $0420, so the pickup inherits the dead enemy's position through CopyActorState): value 1 = SpawnDropGem1 (fixed $83), value 2 = SpawnDropGem2 (fixed $84), any other nonzero value (3) = SpawnDropByHpTier (random, see below).

=== THE PICKUP ===

The actor carries its item id in chatPtr ($7F000A,X) and has the 'friendly' flag $0020 in its $10 (from the spawn flags). When the player overlaps it, combat_collision.InteractionDamage_NPCChat calls GiveItemToPlayer(chatPtr) and turns the actor into NpcDespawnStub. Ids: $83 = 1 gem, $84 = 2 gems, $85 = 5 gems (cap 999), $86 = hpToHeal += 5 (UpdateHUD refills 1 HP every 8 frames) plus the spark effect and SFX $22.
Each entry also spawns a marked child, interaction_handlers.collect_handler_gem (flags $2700), which pulls the pickup toward the player while L / R is held. The pickup is the marked parent ($12 bit $0040 set by SpawnAfterMarked), so its Die also removes the child. Each body clears $10 bit $0400 that the $0420 spawn flags set (see OQ-I049-3).

=== LIFETIME (spriteset_enemies animation lists) ===

Gems: anim 4 / 5 / 6 (gems $83 / $84 / $85) for 10 passes (about 75 ticks each: a 60-tick still frame and 5 shimmer frames of 3 ticks, about 750 ticks), then the blink anim 9 / $0A / $0B for 150 passes (2 ticks each, about 300 ticks), then Die. Heal: anim $22 for 180 passes (2 ticks, about 360 ticks), then anim $35 for 60 passes (4 ticks, about 240 ticks), then Die.

=== WEIGHTED DROP (SpawnDropByHpTier) ===

HP tier by the player's HP against max HP: HP <= max/4 uses table group $20, HP <= max/2 uses group $10, otherwise group 0. A random byte is compared against the group's four ascending thresholds (the last is $0100, so it always matches) and the first row whose threshold is above the byte gives the body to run. Probabilities of 256 outcomes:
HP above half: $86 heal 5.9%, $85 5 gems 17.6%, $84 2 gems 36.3%, $83 1 gem 40.2%. HP between a quarter and a half: $85 9.8%, $83 19.9%, $86 30.1%, $84 40.2%. HP at or below a quarter: $84 4.7%, $83 15.2%, $85 29.7%, $86 50.4%. The heal becomes the likeliest drop when the player is low on HP.

thinkers/global_ambient_dispatcher.asm.blockNote:
Per-scene hub thinker (Bank 00, 49035-49577, about 545 bytes), spawned in about 60 scene_thinkers lists, usually as the last slot. It has two jobs: it loads the player's sprite palette for the current form once at spawn, and it runs the shared 'talk to the thing in front of you' interaction every frame. It is not an ambient effect, and the trigger is the interact bit of joypadCurrent, not a direction press as the old header said.

=== PALETTE (spawn only) ===

SwitchCase on characterForm ($0AD4: 0 Will, 1 Freedan, 2 Shadow; no range check, so the table's fourth entry is never reached) runs PaletteStart / PaletteStep on bundle #0B (Will), #0C (Freedan) or #23 (Shadow). All three write colours $81-$8F, which is OBJ palette 0 colours 1-15, the player's sprite palette. #0B and #0C are a single static strip; #23 is an animated set of strips (wait 2 each). PaletteStep plays the whole bundle before the script continues. The palette is chosen once when the thinker spawns, so a form change in the middle of a scene is not re-applied until the next scene setup.

=== FILTER WORD ===

thinker-def <#00, #08> gives animScratch2 = $0800 (bit 11 set: also run in the Light runners). GlobalAmbientInteractEntry clears bit 11 in the thinker's own animScratch2, so from then on the dispatcher runs only in RunThinkers_General (the main loop) and is skipped by the lighter frame routines (dialogue, render, music upload): no new talk starts while a dialogue frame loop is running. The old comment called bit 11 an 'interaction ready flag'.

=== TALK INTERACTION (every frame) ===

1. PHD / TCD set D = 0 and joypadCurrent bit $8000 is tested: the interact bit. In the vanilla layout it is the B button (remapB); in this build transforms.json rewrites the system_init defaults to remapA = $8080 and remapB = $4008, so the A button feeds it (together with the attack bit $0080). The notes in this file name the logical bit, not a button. Not pressed: return.
2. GetPlayerFacingDirection: carry SET = no valid facing, return; carry CLEAR = valid (GlobalAmbientFacingValid; the old label said Invalid). A = 0 down, 1 up, 2 left, 3 right, saved in $09EE.
3. A probe point one pixel in front of the player ($18 / $1C = player X / Y plus (0,+1), (0,-1), (-1,0) or (+1,0)) is built. The four probe labels follow the facing code: GlobalAmbientProbeDown handles facing 0 (down), GlobalAmbientProbeUp facing 1 (up), GlobalAmbientProbeLeft facing 2 (left), GlobalAmbientProbeRight facing 3 (right); the old ScanEast / ScanWest / ScanNorth / ScanSouth labels were rotated against these.
4. GlobalAmbientFindActorInFront walks the actor list from actorListFirst and keeps the actor with the smallest |dx| + |dy| to the probe point whose |dx| and |dy| are both below $10 and whose sum is below $20. Only actors with Flags10 bit $1000 count (the third actor-def header byte of NPCs and objects carries it; the player has it clear and is skipped). X = 0 when none is found.
5. The target is 'in front' when its coordinate along the facing axis is beyond the probe (GlobalAmbientTargetInRange), otherwise it is at or behind the player (GlobalAmbientTargetAtOrBehind). Both need a non-zero chatPtr ($7F000A, set by SetInteractHandler). A target at or behind the player runs its chat routine directly; a target in front first sets the interact bit in joypadHeld.
6. In front and Flags12 ($12) bit $0200 clear: the turn-and-talk path (GlobalAmbientTalkWithSnapshot; it plays no sound, which the old label TalkSound suggested). The target's actor slot ($30 bytes, bank 0) and its extended $7F page ($30 bytes) are copied to $7E:3410-$346F through the RAM MVN stub at $0402 ($0404 = destination bank, $0405 = source bank, A = $2F is the byte count minus one, not a sound number; the old comments called it SFX $2F). The target is then turned to face the player (GlobalAmbientPickTalkAnimFrame), its animation is updated at once, its chat routine runs as a subroutine and, when it returns, both copies are written back (GlobalAmbientTalkRestoreActor). WRAM flags, dialogue and inventory changes made by the chat routine persist, but the NPC's own actor fields (position, animation, entry pointer, flags) are put back as they were; the next-link $06 is kept as it is now when the saved copy had none (it was the list tail).
7. Flags12 bit $0200 set (over 150 NPC, sign, book and door actor scripts set it) skips the snapshot, the turn and the animation: the chat routine runs directly (GlobalAmbientDeferToScript).
8. GlobalAmbientClearTalkInput then clears the interact bit in joypadCurrent and sets it in joypadHeld so the same press cannot trigger again.

GlobalAmbientPickTalkAnimFrame turns the target to face the player: it picks offset 0 down, 1 up, 2 left, 3 right of the target's 8-frame animation group, the OPPOSITE of the player's facing, and adds it to the group base ((index - 2) AND $FFF8) + 2. It overwrites $09EE with that offset; the label GlobalAmbientAnimFacingHorizontal is the left / right branch.

The interaction code uses the global direct page scratch $00-$04, $18 and $1C (D = 0); none of those is part of the persistent engine state.

partNotes.GlobalAmbientFacingValid: Valid-facing path (BCC after GetPlayerFacingDirection: carry clear = valid; the old label said Invalid). Saves the facing in $09EE and splits into the four probe builders.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientProbeDown: Facing 0 = down (the old label said ScanEast): probe point = player X, player Y + 1.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientProbeUp: Facing 1 = up (the old label said ScanWest): probe point = player X, player Y - 1.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientProbeLeft: Facing 2 = left (the old label said ScanNorth): probe point = player X - 1, player Y.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientProbeRight: Facing 3 = right (the old label said ScanSouth): probe point = player X + 1, player Y.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientAnimFacingHorizontal: The LEFT / RIGHT branch (facing 2 or 3; the old label said Vertical): 2 -> offset 3, 3 -> offset 2.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientOnInteractPress: Interact bit pressed (the old label said direction press). Read the player's facing, build the probe point in front of the player and find the interactable actor there.

comments.49112: Carry clear = valid facing: continue at GlobalAmbientFacingValid; carry set: leave
comments.49359: Return address: GlobalAmbientTalkRestoreActor writes the snapshot back after the chat routine returns
comments.49544: Bit 1 set = left / right (the label ...Horizontal is this branch)

thinkers/gold_ship_wreck_palette.asm.blockNote:
Palette-phase thinker of the Gold Ship wreck scenes (Bank 00, 46705-46802). The old name (incan_ruins_transform_palette) and notes said 'Incan Ruins', but the three scene_thinkers lists that spawn it are $2B (ship wreck), $2D (ship wreck interior) and $2F (adrift), all Gold Ship scenes, and the flags it reads, $4D and $52, are set and cleared by dc2F_adrift (also gs2E_sleep and gs2B_erik). The old doc claims about Larai Cliff / Angkor and scene indexes 34-36 are wrong.

=== PHASE PICK (spawn only) ===

The two flag tests run once when the thinker spawns; the loops after them never return to the tests, so the phase is fixed for the scene visit (scene $2F reloads for each adrift 'day', which re-spawns the thinker with the then-current flags). Flag $52 set: final phase. Else flag $4D set: GoldShipWreckPaletteFlag4D (bundle #34 once, then the #33 loop). Neither: default.

=== DEFAULT: bundle #1A forever ===

A 12-strip palette cycle on colours $21-$2C (palette 2, colours 1-12): each strip is a 24-byte window that slides one colour at a time (wait 2-5), the peak colour $4164 a bright blue, so a highlight travels through the 12 colours. PaletteStart + PaletteStep play all strips and BRA repeats. It reads as a water glint cycle (an inference from the colours).

=== FLAG $4D: GoldShipWreckPaletteFlag4D ===

Bundle #34 once (a one-shot: 16 colours at $70, palette 7, and one colour at $59), then the scene-setup latch $FF is set and bundle #33 (the same 12-strip cycle as #1A with other colour values) loops while $FF stays set. When the latch is cleared (next scene setup or inventory open) the thinker restarts with #34. The old note 'alternate between #34 and #33' is wrong: #34 plays once per latch cycle.

=== FLAG $52: GoldShipWreckPaletteFlag52 ===

Kills the thinker at the list head ($5A) and the one in the next pool slot (+$10): the first two thinkers spawned, which are scanline_band_hdma_thinker records 0 and 1 in all three lists (pool slots are handed out in ascending order from $0F00). KillThinker works on the slot in X and uses D only for its operand pointer, so D can stay on this thinker. Then it fills palette-buffer bytes $7F0A40-$7F0A5F, colours $20-$2F (palette 2), with $1421 (very dark blue, R1 G1 B5) so the colours the cycle used stay flat, sets colour 0 ($7F0A00) to $1442, applies bundle #36 (17 colours at $50, 16 at $70), sets $FF and waits for the latch to clear before repeating the fill and #36 (the kills are not repeated). The old 'CGRAM entries $40-$5F' are buffer byte offsets.

What $4D and $52 mean in story terms (adrift day / night / starvation phase) and what the colours depict is not decoded (OQ-I044-1).

actors/hit_stagger_controller.asm.blockNote:
Hit knockback and recovery controller (Bank 00, 55415-55927). One short-lived actor is spawned per hit. It slides the victim along one axis for 16 frames by moving ITSELF (collision-checked movement) and copying its position to the victim every frame, then either hands control back (player) or resolves the hit (enemy: HP check, hit / death callback). It has no sprite and is never placed by a scene.

=== SPAWN CONTRACT ===

Four spawn sites: ApplyPlayerHitstun and combat_collision.ApplyInteractionDamage (flags word $2400, victim = the player) and the two enemy-hit paths in combat_collision (flags $2000). The flags word becomes the child's $10: $2000 = script-driven run path (own wait counter; actor_execution moves such an actor only while $12 bit 3 is set), $0400 = 'the victim is the player': the controller tests it to choose HitStaggerReleasePlayer instead of HitStaggerResolveHit (the old note said $0400 marks an enemy and that the old label HitStaggerReturnAI 're-enables AI for enemies'; HitStaggerReleasePlayer only ever handles the player). CopyActorState gives the child the victim's position, anim index, $12 (without $1000) and, in $24, the victim's slot. The spawner then stores a direction code in the child's $28 and zeroes its $2C / $2E, and copies the victim's extendedFlags bit $0020 ('hitstun skip' in the WRAM map) into the child.
Direction code in $28: 0 = south, 1 = north, 2 = west, 3 = east (CalcKnockbackDirection), 4 or more = no knockback. free101C ($7F101C) of the victim is a knockback TIER: 0 for ordinary actors, 1 for the player (player_character init) and mu5F_cyclops; the only writers in extracted/ are CopyActorState (zero), those three and this file (copy to the child).

=== HitStaggerMain ===

$10 |= $0008 (collision-checked movement) unless the victim has extendedFlags $0020; $12 |= $0008 (movement request for a script-driven actor). If $12 bit $0010 is set (inherited from the victim: stagger-immune in combat_collision) or the direction code is 4 or more, there is no knockback: WaitByte #$0F (16 ticks), then HitStaggerReleasePlayer (player) or HitStaggerResolveHit. Otherwise the victim's pixel X / Y are saved in orbitAngle / orbitDiameter ($7F0010 / $7F0012: no orbit here, the words are reused as the START position), the tier is copied, and the direction code is decoded by chained DEC / BMI (the old note spoke of a '3-deep stack-encoded direction index'; there is no such stack): 0 = Y chain (carry set), 1 = Y chain with ForceDirBoth (negated), 2 = X chain with ForceDirBoth, 3 = X chain (carry clear). Each branch first clears the inherited ForceDir bits ($6000 of $12). The branches JSR HitStaggerApplyKnockbackDelta, which pushes HitStaggerStoreMovementDelta as a return address; that routine stores the movement chain head in $2E (carry set, $26 := 0, vertical) or $2C (carry clear, $26 := 1, horizontal; the old doc had the axis flag the other way round). The RTS chain ends in HitStaggerSlideLoop (pushed by Main).
Curves (movement_delta_table, one delta per frame, pixels): tier 0 uses entry $22 = 4 4 5 5 5 5 4 4 3 3 2 2 1 1 0 (sum 48 px = 3 tiles); tier 1 and above use entry $23 = 3 3 4 4 3 3 2 2 2 2 1 1 1 1 0 (sum 32 px = 2 tiles). The player is tier 1.

=== HitStaggerSlideLoop (the 16-frame slide loop) ===

SetEntryHereAndYield, then LoopStart #$10: 16 frames in which the child's $14 / $16 are copied into the victim. After the loop: the player ($10 bit $0400) goes to HitStaggerReleasePlayer. An enemy without $10 bit $0008 goes straight to ResolveHit. Otherwise the distance travelled along the axis ($26 = 0: Y, else X) is d = |start - current|: d = 0 resolves at once; if d is a multiple of 16 HitStaggerCheckKnockbackDistance compares it with the tier threshold (tier 0 $30, tier 1 $20, tier 2 and above $40) and carry CLEAR (equal = the full slide happened) resolves; any other d is a CUT-SHORT slide (a wall stopped it): the victim's chain pointer and delta word on the knocked axis are zeroed ($2E and $7F002E for a vertical slide, $2C and $7F002C for a horizontal one) and its wait counter $08 is zeroed when it has no chain on the other axis, so its script resumes immediately (purpose inferred, OQ-I046-3). The thresholds equal the curve sums (48 and 32), which is why a full slide matches exactly; tiers 2 and 3 use the 32-px curve with a $40 threshold and could never match (no actor uses them).

=== HitStaggerResolveHit (enemy) ===

HP ($7F0026) nonzero: if onHitCallback ($7F1000) is set it becomes the victim's entry address (low word only, the bank word is unchanged) and is cleared; the victim's iframe counter becomes $FFF4 (-12, recovery). HP zero: the victim's $10 gets $0040 (dead) unless it already has it, its entry becomes onDeathCallback / onDeathCallbackBank when set (and $08, $2C, $2E are zeroed) or StandardEnemyDefeatHandler in the same bank. Finally X := D (the child) and COP Die, because the COP needs X = the actor slot.

=== HitStaggerReleasePlayer (player only) ===

Unless playerFlags has $0A00 (game over / script lock) the player's entry address becomes player_character.PlayerIdleEntry. The player's iframe counter is set to $FFE2 (-30) and the D-pad bits $0F00 of joypadMaskStd are cleared (shown again). Because a positive counter freezes the player controller, overwriting the $003C that ApplyPlayerHitstun wrote ends the stun after the 16-frame slide (about 17 ticks), not after 60; a heavy hit's -60 is likewise shortened to -30.

=== Helpers ===

HitStaggerCheckKnockbackDistance stores d in the absolute scratch $0000 and pushes HitStaggerZeroToCarry - 1, so the CMP's RTS lands in HitStaggerZeroToCarry, which turns Z into carry (CLC when equal, SEC otherwise). All operands written with four hex digits ($0000, $002C, $002E, $0008 ...) are absolute addresses; $0000 is the global scratch word, the others are the slot fields indexed by X.

Everything here is UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME (no emulator trace); the arithmetic and flow are read from the code and the movement_delta_table nodes.

partNotes.HitStaggerSlideLoop: The 16-frame slide loop (not a direction picker): the child moves, the victim copies its position every frame. Afterwards: player to HitStaggerReleasePlayer, enemy to the distance check and ResolveHit.
partNotes.HitStaggerReleasePlayer: Player only: PlayerIdleEntry as the entry address (unless game over or script lock), iframe counter $FFE2, D-pad shown again, Die. No AI is restored (the old label said HitStaggerReturnAI).
partNotes.loc_00D8C6: No knockback: wait 16 ticks, then HitStaggerReleasePlayer when the victim is the player ($10 bit $0400), else ResolveHit.

actors/player/shadow_shimmer.asm.blockNote:
Shadow's palette shimmer (Bank 02, 176654-176798): a hidden companion that animates the player's OBJ palette 0 (colours $81-$8F) while the player is Shadow (characterForm 2).

SPAWN: PlayerCharacterDef (SpawnListAppend, so it is appended at the end of the actor list) and the two Dark Space transformations in sE6_gaia (Transform_WillToShadow, Transform_FreedanToShadow), which spawn it just before they set characterForm = 2; the new actor runs later in the same tick, after the form is set. All three use flags $2800: hidden ($2000) plus $0800, so it also runs in the cutscene-only passes. Init dies at once when characterForm is not 2.

STRUCTURE: Init spawns ShadowShimmerSlowStrips with SpawnAfterMarked (a marked child dies with its parent). This actor never touches the palette: it only points the child at one of three routines by writing the child's entry word ($0000,Y) and clearing its waitCounter ($0008,Y). The child is found through $06 (the actor-list successor), which is the child because SpawnAfter inserts it directly behind its spawner.
  - ShadowShimmerSlowStrips: bundle #23 in a loop (eight strips, wait 2 each)
  - ShadowShimmerFastStrips: bundle #24 in a loop (eight strips, waits 0 and 1 alternating: a faster cycle)
  - ShadowShimmerNop: yields every frame, no palette change
Both bundles write colours $81-$8F (15 colours, size byte $1D); bundle #23 is also the Shadow palette that global_ambient_dispatcher loads at spawn.

STATES: Idle (the slow strips, ShadowShimmerSlowStrips) and Active (the fast strips, ShadowShimmerFastStrips). Idle -> Active when playerSpeedEw or playerSpeedNs is nonzero, or when flag byte #00 is set. Active -> Idle when both speeds are zero and flag #00 is clear. The speed words are not set by ordinary walking (walking uses the joypad velocity of player_move_controller); they are nonzero during slope and ramp slides and in run / slide moves, so the fast strips play then. Flag #00 is a general per-scene flag (scene_lifecycle clears it at scene setup; scene_flag_init sets it in 26 scene lists; some scripts set and clear it) that player_character also reads to pick Shadow's idle, ladder and shimmy-detach sprites; where it is set, this actor stays in Active. What the flag means is open (OQ-I030-1; here OQ-I048-1).

GUARD (ShadowShimmerGuard, called every frame from both states): characterForm no longer 2 -> pop the return address and Die (the marked child dies too). Player Flags10 bit $0040 (dead: set when HP reaches 0 by combat_collision and by GameOverSequence; combat_collision also calls it the orb state) -> point the child at ShadowShimmerNop and run SetEntryHere + RTL. The saved entry is that RTL, so the states are never run again for the rest of the scene visit and the palette stays on whatever strip was showing.

partNotes.ShadowShimmerActive: Active state: point the child at the fast strips (ShadowShimmerFastStrips) and restart it, then each frame: guard, stay while a speed word is nonzero, go back to Idle when both are zero and flag byte #00 is clear.
partNotes.ShadowShimmerIdle: Idle state: point the child at the slow strips (ShadowShimmerSlowStrips) and restart it, then each frame: guard, then switch to Active when a speed word is nonzero or flag byte #00 is set. Plain walking leaves both speed words at zero.
partNotes.ShadowShimmerInit: Spawned by PlayerCharacterDef and by the two Dark Space transformations to Shadow. Dies at once unless characterForm is 2, otherwise spawns the palette child (slow strips) and falls into ShadowShimmerIdle.

comments.176664: Spawn the palette child (slow strips, flags $2800); marked, so it dies with this actor

actors/player/slope_ramp_physics.asm.blockNote:
Slope/ramp terrain physics and flat-ground deceleration - SpawnAfter companion of the player actor (177195-178099, Bank 02).

PlayerCharacterDef spawns it with SpawnAfter, so it sits right behind the player actor in the actor list and runs every frame after the player's own scripts. It never moves the player. It only edits playerSpeedEw / playerSpeedNs (and the playerFlags $1000 latch); player_move_controller turns those speeds into movement (speed x 4 plus external velocity) in the same frame: the actor list order is attack, player, slope, controller, so the controller runs right after this actor.

=== FRAME FLOW (SlopePhysicsEntry) ===

1. Gate: if the player actor's $10 has bit $0080 or bit $0040 set (hit marker / orb state) and iframeCounter is not negative, slope detection is skipped and only SlopeFlatDecelerate runs.
2. Speed nonzero (EW or NS): probe the collision tile at (actor X, actor Y - 8) with TileProbeMain, look the type up in SlopeTileDispatch and jump to the handler. A type with no handler goes to the transition-tile test (below), otherwise to SlopeFlatExit.
3. Speed zero and playerFlags $1000 set: reset both step counters and probe four cells (below). A slope found runs its handler, none goes to SlopeFlatExit.
4. Speed zero and no latch: SlopeFlatDecelerate.
A slope handler adds one curve value to one axis (ApplySlopeCurve*) and returns through ClampSpeeds.

=== TILE TYPES (SlopeTileDispatch) ===

| Type | Handler | Pushes the player | Curve |
|------|---------|-------------------|-------|
| $03  | SlopeType03Handler | south (NS +) | slopeCurvePtrB |
| $05  | SlopeType05Handler | west (EW -) | slopeCurvePtrA, negated |
| $0A  | SlopeType0AHandler | east (EW +) | slopeCurvePtrA |
| $0C  | SlopeType0CHandler | north (NS -) | slopeCurvePtrB, negated |

All other types (0-2, 4, 6-9, B, D-F) have a zero entry: no slope. The table holds the handler addresses; the dispatch does DEC, PHA, RTS so that the RTS lands on the handler. Whether a handler pushes DOWNHILL was not checked against the map art; the direction column is what the code does to the speed.

=== CURVES ===

slopeCurvePtrA ($09BA, east-west) and slopeCurvePtrB ($09BC, north-south) both point at the start of the math_lookup_tables block, and decelCurvePtr ($09C2) at that block + $20; system_core sets them once at boot. Each curve is 16 words, read as (counter & $0F) x 2 bytes from the pointer. Default slope curve: $0001 at steps 0, 4, 8 and 12, otherwise 0, i.e. +1 speed unit every fourth frame. Default deceleration curve: $0001 at steps 7 and 15. slopeStepCounter ($09B6) advances once per frame on a slope and is cleared when the slope speed reaches zero, when SlopeFlatExit runs and on every frame of the stopped probe (so a slope always starts at step 0). decelStepCounter ($09B8) advances on EVERY ReadDecelerationStep call, including calls that return 0. maxSpeedEw / maxSpeedNs ($09C8 / $09CA) are set to 9 in system_core and not written again in the extracted code; ClampSpeeds limits |speed| to max - 1 = 8.

=== THE $1000 ON-SLOPE LATCH (playerFlags) ===

Set by the ramp walkers (player_move_ramps, player_move_west) while the player traverses a ramp and by these handlers when a slope curve brings an axis speed to exactly zero. Cleared by player_move_controller whenever the EW or the NS speed is nonzero, and by SlopeFlatDecelerate when EW speed is zero. While it is set player_move_controller drops the joypad velocity, DecelerateEW / DecelerateNS return at once, the Aura Barrier cannot be used and the walk code skips its L/R block check. By this reading a player at rest on the latch gets no joypad movement: the four-cell probe finds the slope again, the first curve step (+1 or -1) gives a nonzero speed, and the next controller pass clears the latch.

=== TRANSITION TILES $06 AND $09 ===

If the tile under the probe has no handler but is type $06 or $09, the code looks at two other cells with MapCellDown (one map row below the probe tile) and then MapCellUp (one row above), both relative to the index TileProbeMain left in $00. A type $05 or $0A in either cell runs that handler; otherwise SlopeFlatExit. The earlier text said "right and left adjacent cells"; MapCellDown/Up step by rows (+/-$10), MapCellRight/Left by columns.

=== STOPPED-ON-SLOPE PROBE ===

Four cells are tested in this order: the probe cell, the cell to its RIGHT (MapCellRight), the cell BELOW it (MapCellDown) and the cell below-right (MapCellRight from the new base; the code stores the new index in $00 after MapCellDown). The first slope type found runs its handler. The probe point here is playerXPos / playerYPos (camera_scroll_controller writes actor X - 8 and actor Y - $10 there), while the moving probe uses (actor X, actor Y - 8); the two phases therefore look at different points (open question).

=== DECELERATION (SlopeFlatDecelerate, DecelerateEW / DecelerateNS) ===

SlopeFlatDecelerate decelerates the EW axis when EW speed is nonzero and then returns; the NS axis is only handled on a frame in which EW speed is already zero (after clearing the $1000 latch). Per axis: skipped while the latch is set; |speed| < 3 is set to zero at once (the step counter is not reset); otherwise a D-pad bit for the direction of travel suppresses deceleration, else one curve value is subtracted (added for negative speeds) and, whether that step was applied or returned 0, a D-pad bit for the opposite direction applies a second curve value (braking). Reaching zero resets decelStepCounter in the EW routine; the NS routine resets slopeStepCounter instead (probable copy slip, open question).

=== OTHER QUIRKS (open questions) ===

ClampSpeeds examines the NS speed only when EW speed is zero. ReadDecelerationStepNS is a byte-for-byte copy of ReadDecelerationStep (same counter, same curve). slopeFracAccum ($09C6) is the sub-pixel accumulator of the north/south slope walkers (player_move_south, player_move_ns); this file only clears it (SlopeFlatExit), as player_move_controller does when the NS speed is zero.

partNotes.CompanionDotMovement:
Per-companion dot actor — move to formation position and animate.

Entry: stores the companion's assigned diameter ($26) into orbitDiameter and position pair ($24) into orbitAngle. Extracts low byte as X offset + cameraTargetX → moveXAlt, high byte as Y offset + cameraTargetY → moveYAlt. MoveToward(#FF, #01) to glide toward the target: #FF is the animation operand (keep the animation), the speed is 1 px per frame.

=== SHARED ANIMATION LOOP (loc_03A497) ===

SetEntryHere → AnimOneFrame → capture frame counter from $08 into $26 (animation timer). Each tick: recompute position from $24 (low byte = X offset + cameraTargetX → $14, high byte via XBA = Y offset + cameraTargetY → $16).

If route active ($0D5A ≠ 0): decrement $26 timer; when negative, loop back to loc_03A497 for another animation cycle. When timer still positive, yield (RTL).

If route done ($0D5A = 0): compute home position from orbitDiameter (X component + cameraTargetX → moveXAlt, Y from $7F0013 + cameraTargetY → moveYAlt). If already at home position (both X and Y match) → Die. Otherwise MoveToward(#FF, #01) one more step toward home, then Die.

comments.238733: Glide toward target: #FF = animation operand (keep it), 1 px per frame

partNotes.StatueRewardNotThisStatue: A statue that is not the one being awarded (match byte differs from globalScriptIndex, and its own flag is still clear): restores X and idles hidden. (The old label StatueRewardWrongTab borrowed 'tab' from the inventory slot logic; there is no tab in scene $FD.)
partNotes.StatueRewardEntry: Actor entry (flow steps 1 and 2 of the block note): joypadMaskStd |= $FFFC (every button hidden), NudgePosition (8, 8), metasprite and flags setup, then the direct screen register writes.

partNotes.DarkSpaceRestoreControl:
Restore player control after transformation — resets entry point to PlayerIdleEntry,
clears movement overrides, restores collision-checked movement (Flags10 bit $0008), unmasks joypad, clears ability-active flag.

comments.587509: Set bit 3: collision-checked movement (vine, ladder and shimmy states clear it)

partNotes.EnemyGemDropRouter:
Gem-type dispatcher called from StandardEnemyDefeatHandler when the enemy's stats byte at offset $03 is nonzero and scene flag $0300 is clear.

A holds the enemy's stat byte +3 (gemDropType, loaded with AND #$00FF just before the JMP): two DEC operations select among three EnemyDropSystem spawn targets (1 = SpawnDropGem1, fixed $83; 2 = SpawnDropGem2, fixed $84; otherwise SpawnDropByHpTier, the weighted picker). Each path spawns the pickup with COP SpawnListAppend (flags $0420) and then jumps back for the remainder of the defeat sequence.

comments.56667: A = enemy stat byte +3 (gemDropType): 1 = fixed $83 gem, 2 = fixed $84 gem, otherwise the weighted picker

comments.181183: Spawn shadow_shimmer with SpawnListAppend (appended at the actor list end) (Shadow palette shimmer, dies if not form 2)

partNotes.PlayerMoveNotStunned: Passed the hit-stun gate (the iframe counter is not running, or it is negative = recovery after a hit): restore X and go on to the lock test.
partNotes.PlayerMoveSync: Stage 3 (sync), X part: if the player actor's pixel X differs from local X >> 2 (a script, COP or knockback moved the player), adopt the actor's X x 4; the old fraction is lost.
partNotes.PlayerMoveSyncY: Stage 3 (sync), Y part: the same comparison and adoption for Y.
partNotes.PlayerMoveJoypadGate: Stage 4 start: playerFlags $1000 (on-slope latch) or $2000 (guard / channel stance) forces the packed joypad velocity to zero; otherwise the pad is read at PlayerMoveReadPad.
partNotes.PlayerMoveReadPad: JoypadToVelocity returns the packed joypad velocity (high byte Y, low byte X).
partNotes.PlayerMoveAxisX: X axis of stage 4: keep the packed velocity on the stack, hand local X to the tick in $22, clear $20. Speed word playerSpeedEw zero: joypad X (sign-extended low byte) plus extVelocityX. Nonzero: speed x 4 plus extVelocityX, and the on-slope latch $1000 is cleared.
partNotes.PlayerMoveAxisY: Y axis of stage 4: consume extVelocityX, hand local Y to the tick in $26, clear $24. Speed word playerSpeedNs zero: slopeFracAccum is zeroed and the velocity is joypad Y (high byte, sign-extended) plus extVelocityY. Nonzero: speed x 4 plus extVelocityY, and the on-slope latch is cleared.
partNotes.PlayerMoveCollisionStage: Stage 5 (move): consume extVelocityY and drop the packed pad velocity. Player Flags10 bit $0008 (collision-checked movement) set: PlayerMoveCollisionTick. Clear (vine, ladder, shimmy): $22 += $20 and $26 += $24 directly, no collision, then the write-back.
partNotes.PlayerMoveCollisionTick: Collision-checked move: store this actor's slot in the scratch word $000A (the tick reads X from it) and JSL player_move_main.PlayerMovementTick, which moves $22 / $26 against the tile map and sets bit $0004 of this actor's $10 on a solid contact.
partNotes.PlayerMoveWriteBack: Stage 6: local position := $22 / $26, the player actor's pixel X / Y := position >> 2, and bit $0004 (solid contact this tick) is copied from this actor's $10 into the player's $10.
partNotes.JoypadVelocityLeft: Left held (Left wins over Right): neither Up nor Down goes to JoypadVelocityPureLeft, Up goes to JoypadVelocityUpLeft, otherwise Down + Left: Y = +6, X = -6.
partNotes.JoypadVelocityRight: Right held (Left clear): the same structure as the left handler: neither vertical bit goes to JoypadVelocityPureRight, Up goes to JoypadVelocityUpRight, otherwise Down + Right: Y = +6, X = +6.
partNotes.JoypadVelocityPureUp: Up held with Left and Right clear: Y = -8, X = 0; restores P and returns directly.
partNotes.JoypadVelocityPureDown: Down held with Left, Right and Up clear: Y = +8, X = 0; restores P and returns directly.
partNotes.JoypadVelocityDone: Exit of the left handlers and of the no-direction case: restore P and return with the packed velocity (Y in the high byte, X in the low byte).
partNotes.JoypadVelocityDoneRight: Exit of the right handlers: restore P and return (same as JoypadVelocityDone).

partNotes.InventoryStatueSlotEntry: Actor entry: NudgePosition (+8, +8), metasprite inventory_spritemap, spawn parameter kept in $24, and an extra 8 px up when bit 4 of the parameter marks a top-row pedestal.
partNotes.InventoryStatueSlotSetup: Parameter handled: $0E := $2000 (the OAM attribute word), then the statue's event flag is read from statue_reward_table (index = low nibble of $24, 4 bytes per entry) and tested with TestFlagRaw.
partNotes.InventoryStatueSlotUncollected: Flag clear (statue not collected yet): restore the actor slot and Die; nothing is drawn.
partNotes.InventoryStatueSlotHide: Status tab (inventoryTabIndex = 3): set the hidden bit $2000 in $10 and return; every other tab clears it in the lines above.

partNotes.HpIncreaseStore: Store point of e_hp_increase: max HP := the new value (the BVC skips the $0255 clamp unless the sum overflowed), hpToHeal := new max HP - current HP, print the message and Die.
partNotes.StrIncreaseStore: Store point of e_str_increase: STR := the new value (the BVC skips the $0255 clamp unless the sum overflowed), print 'Your STR (Strength) has increased!' and Die.
partNotes.DefIncreaseStore: Store point of e_def_increase: DEF := the new value (the BVC skips the $0255 clamp unless the sum overflowed), print 'Your DEF (Defense) has increased!' and Die.
